purpose: Empty capital slipway background for a separately rendered, interchangeable 3D capital-ship model.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: reusable opaque 16:9 landscape background plate for the Capital Slipway construction screen in Stellar Syndicates.
Primary request: an immersive close-up view from inside an EMPTY capital-ship construction slipway in orbit, leaving a broad clear volume for the game's actual interchangeable 3D capital-ship model. Absolutely no spacecraft or ship parts are painted into the background.

Input image 1 is the CAPITAL SLIPWAY architecture reference. Preserve its distinctive one exceptionally long open construction cradle, TWO massive segmented exterior trusses, THREE widely spaced monumental pale-gray gantry frames, a compact rear service/control pod, and paired dark heat-radiator banks. Its structure has heavier beams, longer spans, and more substantial engineering than the ordinary orbital shipyard.
Input image 2 is the previously created EMPTY ORBITAL SHIPYARD background, used only for the shared material style, quality, lighting language and clear compositing space. Make a distinctly larger capital slipway, not a duplicate of that background.

Camera and composition: wide full-bleed landscape 16:9, elevated three-quarter inspection viewpoint from beside the near service gantry, looking diagonally down the exceptionally long empty berth. This is a close environment view with crisp nearby metalwork and strong architectural depth, not a distant sprite of the whole station. A colossal near gantry frames the top and outer sides; a second and third gantry recede far along the same axis, their uprights positioned toward the picture's outside edges. Two long heavily reinforced parallel truss spines and their service catwalks border the lower left and lower right perimeter. Repeated small work lights, layered truss segments, narrow service walkways and tiny windows on the distant control pod communicate monumental scale. No people are needed for scale.

CRITICAL: preserve a wide uninterrupted empty central volume, approximately the middle 70 percent of the image width and middle 60 percent of its height, where a dreadnought, titan or other selected ship will later be rendered in 3D. Keep structural beams, clamps, arms, scaffolding, cables and railings outside that placement zone. The center should remain mostly quiet dark neutral vacuum with sparse subdued stars. Low distant supports may frame its far edge but must not cut across the future ship silhouette. Park all heavy adjustable clamp carriages outward along the perimeter rails, with their jaws folded down or away. Retract cranes near the overhead border. No fixed narrow ship-shaped cradle and no painted shadow of a missing hull.

Orbital setting: exposed vacuum through the long open berth and sides. There is no ground-like floor under the cradle, no enclosed terrestrial hangar, no nearby planet dictating a particular world, and no bright nebula dominating the center. At the far outer edge, the service/control pod has small amber-lit windows and large dark paired radiator panels. Reinforced segmented beams, sturdy joint housings, yellow heavy-lift equipment, recessed utility conduits and redundant exterior rails give the capital facility its own identity.

Style: polished semi-realistic science-fiction game environment painting with physically convincing industrial geometry and selective fine detail. Match the references' weathered pale gray armor, graphite steel trusses, restrained yellow machinery, amber work lamps and small cyan service indicators. Neutral cool space illumination, warm practical work lights directed inward, readable shadowed surfaces, restrained bloom. The real ship placed later must remain the scene's focal point.

Constraints: a single finished empty background image. No ship, no spacecraft, no partial vessel, no hull skeleton, no engine, no cockpit, no suspended armor panel, no loose ship parts, no welding effects, no crew, no astronauts, no text, no labels, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no UI, no progress bars, no placeholder outline, no placement grid or wireframe, no ground terrain, no floor spanning the central gap, no transparency.
